I changed `anthrouter/handlers.py` so the routed-tier cache is now keyed by the requested model as well as the conversation. I did not reproduce your scenario or add a test for it. The cause below is my reading of the code, not something I confirmed against your request log.

**Cause:** the cache was keyed only by session plus conversation. The `sonnet` turn classified as `trivial` stored `haiku`. A later `opus` request in the same conversation then replayed that cached `haiku` on a continuation turn, such as a tool-result or text-less one. The replay cap (`_cap_cached_tier`) only stops a cached tier from upgrading the request. It deliberately lets a lower tier replace a higher requested model, so `haiku` replacing `opus` was allowed.

**Fix:** the `tier_key` line in `handlers.py` now includes `payload.get('model')`. A tier cached for one requested model is no longer replayed for another, and an `opus` turn in that conversation gets classified on its own.

**Tests:** 1119 passed, 1 skipped, and 1 failed. The failure is `tests/test_config.py::test_editable_fields_live_editable_fields`. It fails the same way with my change stashed, so it is not caused by this fix.

I left the "lower cached tier may downgrade a higher request" cap alone, since its docstring says that is by design. If you also want continuation turns capped at the requested tier, that would be a separate change to `_cap_cached_tier`.
